correctness.rationale: For r>=1, an acyclic total-order orientation starts with the endpoints of a deleted edge; as they are nonadjacent, each vertex reaches at most n-1 vertices including itself. The reverse-order most-preferred unused-reachable-color algorithm with n-1 colors is proper and permits no envy arc against the orientation: an assumed backward envy arc would force a repeated reachable color, contradicting the earlier endpoint choice. Lower bound for r>=2: with q=n-2 colors, each proper color class has size at most 2 and every doubled class must be an absent edge; at least 2 distinct absent pairs must be doubled. On each absent pair impose opposite rankings of q colors. Two doubled classes of colors a != b then have adjacent members that mutually envy and form a 2-cycle. r=1 is forced by clique size n-1; r=0 complete graph has stable chi n; chi ordinary is n-r. Independently enumerated every proper (n-2)-coloring in 9 profiles 4<=n<=8, 2<=r<=floor(n/2): 11,888 colorings and each had the mutual-envy obstruction. The universal quantifiers follow from proof, not enumeration.
residual_risks: The exact lower profile follows from reverse-ranked matched pairs, not arbitrary missing-edge structures.
